mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 or B200 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 or B200 petrol engine typically costs £1,100-£3,200 supply-only, depending on which generation and engine code your car has. M266.960 (W245) units are the most affordable; M270.920 (B250) and M282.914 (W247) command premium pricing. Used engine: £800-£1,800 depending on mileage and condition. Reconditioned engine: £1,300-£2,600. Rebuilt engine: £1,100-£3,200 with 12-month warranty. Fitting adds £400-£800 at a specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 or B200 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning sign on M270 (W246) petrol engines is a rattling noise on cold start, lasting 1-3 seconds. This indicates camshaft adjuster wear or timing chain stretch. Rattling on cold start - the first and most important warning sign. Engine management light with P0011, P0014 or camshaft correlation codes. Loss of power, misfire or rough running. Complete failure leads to chain snap, bent valves and catastrophic engine damage. Warning: Ignoring cold-start rattle on an M270 engine leads to chain snap, bent valves, and a £3,000+ repair bill. Replace the tensioner and adjusters preventatively.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 or B200 petrol have a timing chain or belt?

acceptedAnswer.text: All petrol engines in the Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 and B200 use a timing chain, not a belt. The M266 (W245) uses a single roller chain; the M270 (W246) uses a dual-stage timing chain system; the M282 (W247) uses a chain-driven valvetrain. M266.960: single roller chain, front-mounted. M270.910/M270.920: dual-stage timing chain, front-mounted. M282.914: chain-driven, front-mounted. None of these engines have a cambelt - no scheduled replacement interval, but tensioner and chain wear is common. Cold-start rattle = timing chain or adjuster warning - act immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a high-mileage Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 or B200 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: For W245 models (2005-2011) worth £1,500-£3,500, a rebuilt engine at £1,100-£2,800 often approaches the car's value. However, if the body and transmission are sound, specialist replacement with 12-month warranty can still be cheaper than buying a comparable replacement car. W246 models (2011-2018, worth £4,000-£9,000) and W247 models (2019-present, worth £9,000-£18,000) are almost always worth repairing. W245 (2005-2011): value £1.5k-£3.5k - borderline economical, evaluate carefully. W246 (2011-2018): value £4k-£9k - replacement makes sense. W247 (2019-present): value £9k-£18k - definitely worth replacing. Rebuilt engine (£1.1k-£3.2k fitted) often cheaper than comparable replacement car.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 and B200 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained M266 engines regularly reach 150,000-200,000 miles; M270 engines typically last 150,000-180,000 miles with proper servicing; M282 units are too new for definitive data but expected to match M270 longevity. M266 (W245): 150,000-200,000 miles; oil consumption the main limiter. M270 (W246): 150,000-180,000 miles; camshaft wear and timing chain the primary concerns. M282 (W247): reliability data still emerging; injector seal leaks and carbon buildup the main concerns. Regular oil changes (every 10,000 miles or annually) essential for all petrol engines. Direct-injection M270 and M282 engines benefit from occasional intake valve carbon cleaning.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the B180 and B200 petrol engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B180 and B200 share the same engine family in each generation but are tuned differently. In the W245 (M266), the B180 (1.7L) produces 116bhp while the B200 (2.0L) produces 136bhp. In the W246 (M270.910), the B180 produces 122bhp while the B200 produces 156bhp from the same 1.6L displacement. In the W247 (M282.914), the B180 produces 136bhp while the B200 produces 150-163bhp from the same 1.3L displacement. Same engine family, different state of tune. B180: lower power, better fuel economy. B200: higher power, slightly worse economy. Replacement engines are not interchangeable without ECU remapping.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 / B200 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 and B200 petrol models have served as the core petrol offerings across three generations of the compact MPV. The first-generation W245 (2005-2011) used naturally aspirated M266 engines, the second-generation W246 (2011-2018) introduced turbocharged M270 direct-injection units, and the current W247 (2019-present) features the Renault-derived M282 1.3-litre turbo petrol.

milestones.description: March 2005 - W245 launch: M266.960 2.0L naturally aspirated petrol, 136bhp (B200); B170 (1.7L, 116bhp) and B150 (1.5L, 95bhp) also available
W245 facelift: B180 NGT introduced with M266.960 2.0L bi-fuel (petrol/CNG), 116bhp
B200 Turbo joins range: M266.980 2.0L turbocharged, 193bhp
November 2011 - W246 launch: M270.910 1.6L turbo petrol, 122bhp (B180) and 156bhp (B200)
B250 joins range: M270.920 2.0L turbo petrol, 211bhp
W246 facelift: M270 engines continue with emissions updates
W247 launch: M282.914 1.3L turbo petrol, 136bhp (B180) and 163bhp (B200)
W247 facelift: 48V mild hybrid (MHEV) added to select M282 petrol variants

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 / B200 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 and B200 petrol models are broadly reliable, but each engine family has well-documented failure points. The M266 naturally aspirated units suffer from oil consumption and timing chain stretch at higher mileages. The M270 turbocharged direct-injection engines are prone to camshaft adjuster wear and timing chain issues from 50,000 miles. The current M282 1.3-litre unit has injector seal and carbon buildup concerns. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch & Camshaft Wear - Why the Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 / B200 Petrol M270 Fails Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 / B200 (M270.910, 2011-2018, W246)
problems.rootCause: The M270 dual-stage timing chain system is prone to stretch, while the camshaft adjusters (phasers) suffer from internal wear, causing a rattling noise on cold start. Carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection exacerbates drivability issues. Mercedes issued an updated camshaft actuator (A2700501147) with improved wear resistance.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, tensioner, guides and camshaft adjusters. No engine removal.
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-70k miles if caught early. Suitable only before chain jumps or guides fail.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Cylinder head rebuild, new camshafts, adjusters, valves, intake carbon blasting.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if camshaft has worn through bearings or valves damaged.

problems.rootCause: The M266 naturally aspirated petrol engine suffers from worn piston rings and ageing valve stem seals, allowing oil to seep into the combustion chamber. Oil consumption rates can exceed 1 litre per 750 miles on affected units.

problems.h4: Injector Seal Leaks & Carbon Buildup - Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 / B200 Petrol M282 Engine
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 / B200 (M282.914, 2019-present, W247)
